title: Contemplation by the detail: two aspects, chachma and bina, and the balance of bittul and simcha

lectures.id: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3
Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

overview: Chapter 5 continues the book's teaching on how to contemplate. Before the chain of worlds is studied, a person must know its details, and even when he studies one detail he needs the right balance between the general and the particular. Every contemplation of creation has two aspects: the created *yesh*, which the mind can understand and see nullified to its source, and the *ayin* of G-d that creates it, which is hidden and cannot be grasped. These two are the powers of *chachma* and *bina*. *Chachma* is a seeing, a flash beyond understanding, which brings *bittul*, awe and humility. *Bina* is a hearing, a full grasp, which brings *simcha* at mastery. In *chachma*, the deeper one goes, the more the source is beyond him. The chapter applies this to the *galgalim*, which are external vessels of *Malchus*; to the angels of *Beriya*, which grasp something of their source and express G-d's will, whose essence transcends the *mitzvos*; to the hidden *ayin* of *Asiya*; and to the emanation of *Atzilus*. The two feelings must come together in every detail, in proportion to real understanding. Imagined *bittul* without understanding is a vain fantasy.

terms.gloss: something: the created thing, which the mind can understand and experience directly
nothing: the transcendent G-dly source that creates the yesh, hidden beyond grasp
the seeing: a flash of direct experience beyond understanding, which brings bittul
the hearing: understanding that comes as a full grasp, which brings simcha
the power of the soul by which chachma sees, with the mind's eye and not physical sight
self-nullification; here mainly awe, humility and wonder, the sense of not knowing what one perceives
joy of accomplishment, from having grasped and mastered something
emotional arousal: the feeling that a grasp produces
grasp, comprehension; also, to capture something in the way a work of art captures an idea
the planets, stars and celestial spheres, with their orbits: the external vessels of Malchus
kingship: the way G-d's ability to make us feel independent is expressed
illumination: a reflected light, which shines into the soul of a planet

blocks.text: The class opens by placing the chapter in the book. The last chapter taught how to contemplate, in the general way or the detailed way, and how to combine the two. This chapter takes up a similar balance. Chapters 1 to 3 explain what *hisbonenus* is. Chapters 4 to 6 teach the preparations: the right attitude, the right perspective, and the balance among them. Chapters 7 to 9 introduce the concepts that serve as foundations. These first nine chapters lay the framework for a proper *hisbonenus*.

blocks.text: Before the details comes another introduction, about the quality of contemplation even when one studies a single detail. Here too there must be a balance: the *klal* and the *prat*, the big picture and its small parts. Someone who studies a single detail may come to think he understands it, and he may be like the person who says, "I learned it, I did it even twice", and fools himself into thinking he understands. This is the kind of balance that matters for anyone who truly wants to come close to G-d and not merely fulfill his obligation.

blocks.text: Studying these things has pitfalls, for better or for worse, when a person does not approach them with the right attitude. The result can be counterproductive, or at least less productive than it should be. This chapter is about the right approach.

blocks.text: So there are two things. The first is the *yesh*, the created thing, which the mind can understand and experience. Whenever one studies an idea, there is a part of it that a person can understand and have direct experience in.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Touching something hot
blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe gives an example. When you touch something hot, you directly experience the feeling that it is hot, and you know that intimately. But what heat is, and what causes it, you do not know. People can make theories and models to describe it, yet until fairly recent times it was a mystery, and even now energy is a very abstract thing that is not fully understood. The Alter Rebbe explains almost any experience in this way.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The essence of the soul
blocks.text: We all feel that we are alive and conscious, and we experience that intimately: we can see, hear, feel and have emotions and ideas. But what is the real essence of the soul, and of life? That is beyond our understanding. Whenever we study something, the part we can know and directly experience is the *yesh*, which is created.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The first category, the created *yesh*, is what one learns more of: the more you study it, the more you understand, as in any science. The second category, the abstract source, is not something you do not know because you lack knowledge. It is inherently beyond human knowledge by its nature. The more you learn about it, the more you come to recognize the limits of your understanding, and you gain wonder and humility rather than a sense of accomplishment and mastery.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: Both must be kept. A person who focuses only on the *yesh* and on what he can know becomes haughty, thinking "I understand all these things, I mastered it", and he lacks the humility and awe that come from recognizing how much is beyond him. A person who focuses only on what he cannot know misses the concrete, usable understanding and the mastery. A healthy study needs the balance of the two.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: Tanya on the impurity of secular wisdom
blocks.text: Tanya speaks of a certain impurity associated with secular wisdom. Rabbi Walters thinks a lot of it comes from learning only in the first way: focusing on the *yesh*, on what one can understand, with a certain arrogance. Such learning does not reach the second side, the humility and awe that this is a G-dly thing beyond our understanding, and the balance between the two.

blocks.text: Whenever a person contemplates, he must hold both sides: what he can understand, and the recognition that what he knows is a small example of something transcendent. Tanya says that saying G-d is too great to understand is like saying an idea is so deep you cannot hold it in your hand, which would make people laugh. It is not that it cannot be understood; it is beyond human understanding by its nature.

blocks.text: Back to the first thing. The first is recognizing *bittul hayesh l'ayin*: the actual created *yesh*, and seeing how it is nullified to its source. You still see the G-dliness in the thing, but you are looking at the created thing itself. This is understanding the relationship of a limited, finite thing first, and appreciating how it is created from its source.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: What can be recognized in the created *yesh* is close to the intellect. One can directly see G-d's handiwork in creation, appreciate how the works of creation work, how they are created and how they work together. Through various explanations, examples and metaphors, whatever it takes to understand the creations around us, one sees how they are nullified to their G-dly source and created from it, until it becomes very true to the mind.

blocks.text: In Yiddish he says it really sits in the mind. It becomes completely obvious and intuitive to a person once he studies it. This is like any science: one studies, gains real knowledge and a real mastery, until he really knows it, from direct experience and experiments.

blocks.text: The text now sets out a contrast between two powers. The first is the seeing of *chachma*, the *koach mah* of the soul, which sees not with physical sight but with the sight of the mind's eye, in a flash, beyond complete understanding. The second is the hearing of *bina*, the way of understanding by hearing. The class says this sentence is long and awkward to translate, and that the *chachma* side will be explained first.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: *Koach mah* is the power to have a direct experience of something higher than oneself, in which one has *bittul*. The seeing is not physical. It is the mind's eye, a flash of something beyond full understanding that one can still experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: The emotional effect of this seeing is *bittul*. Generally *bittul* is translated as nullification, but Rabbi Walters thinks that here it is mainly a sense of awe, humility and wonder: one perceives something, yet knows that one does not know it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.text: This humility is the lack of feeling oneself at all. The seeing also draws a person in, so that he loses his sense of self, as when, even, *lehavdil*, a person is just watching a movie and gets drawn into it and loses himself in it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 046 ch 5 part 1.mp3

blocks.title: The Milky Way from a dark place
blocks.text: A person moved from his normal sense of things is so absorbed that he is not even aware he was moved, nor does he think about the experience. This is the awe and wonder he means. Go out where it is dark, away from city lights, and look up to see the Milky Way. Astronauts describe the same awe, looking from the space station at Earth and the stars. So *chachma* gives a person a sense of *bittul*, humility and awe, not a sense that he understood something. It is a powerful, moving experience, and when a person appreciates a reality beyond himself, it is in the way of *bittul*.

blocks.outOfPlace: Class 047 opens by recapping lines 5-21 (class 046) before it reads line 22.
blocks.text: The class opens in the middle of chapter 5 with a recap. When one studies something, there is a part he can understand, and it brings accomplishment, joy and mastery. There is also a part that is beyond understanding, and that should lead to *bittul*, humility, awe and wonder, even a kind of distress that it is beyond him. It is necessary and healthy to have both at once: to master what one can understand, and to accept the limit of one's understanding. The class says it picks up at about the middle of page 224.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Whenever a person studies any detail of the chain of worlds, or any particular example of *yichud*, doing it properly brings him to recognize both aspects in his contemplation: the hidden G-dly source that is beyond understanding, and the revealed creation.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The emotional impact of this is two opposite feelings. On one side, his heart is troubled within him over the very wonder of grasping the G-dly *ayin* that creates everything.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The saying goes that the secrets of this Torah are given only to one whose heart is troubled within him. This is the feeling a person needs: a longing and a bother that he wants to connect and reach beyond what is humanly possible, and yet he recognizes the limit and that there are things he cannot grasp.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: On the one hand, he has total recognition of the transcendence of the G-dly source that creates everything, and of the impossibility of understanding it. On the other hand, he has joy and accomplishment from really understanding the topic: how the created things, in this world and in the higher worlds, come from that source. As we talked about a little yesterday.

sections.title: The galgalim and the angels: outer vessels through which Malchus shows, each nullified to its source
sections.summary: The planets and spheres (*galgalim*) and the angels of *Beriya* are external vessels through which *Malchus* of *Malchus* is expressed. They grasp something of their source, are nullified to it, and express G-d's will, whose essence transcends them.

phrases.en: is only the most external *kli*, the most external aspect of the vessel of *Malchus* of *Asiya*

phrases.en: into what's called the soul of this planet or star or whatever it is

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Take as an example someone meditating on how the *galgalim*, which are the planets and all the celestial bodies and their orbits, are created from their G-dly source. These *galgalim* are the external vessels of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: What is expressed and grasped by these *galgalim*, the planets and spheres and all these things, is only the most external *kli*. It is a reflected light, a light of a light, shining into the soul of each planet or star.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The sun, the moon and the tides
blocks.text: He turns to what the heavens do for us. Nearly all the energy on earth comes from the sun, and the fossil fuels are stored sunlight from plants. The moon brings the main tidal forces, and the sun weaker ones. On the coast the water rises and falls tens of feet, and even the land rises and falls a few inches. The other planets and stars shine on us to a lesser degree, and gamma rays and meteors constantly reach earth.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Stars and the elements
blocks.text: The raw material of the earth is made in stars. A star is like a factory that turns simple protons, or hydrogen, into the other elements. Iron, calcium and carbon, and the atoms of our own bodies, were made in stars, and the heavier ones came from stars exploding as supernovae.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The weather, the seasons and the mazalos
blocks.text: All of this is the idea of the *mazalos*. Night and day, the changing position of the sun relative to the earth, and the length of the days all shape the seasons and the weather, in subtle ways that influence the weather patterns day by day.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The pen, the rock and the paper airplane
blocks.text: The idea of *Malchus* of *Malchus* is that a ruler influences something outside himself, yet does it so that it seems totally independent. Compare writing while still holding the pen, and then handing over the paper, or moving something with your hand versus throwing it, after which the hand can rest. Or a kid in a classroom throws a paper airplane, and all the children sit still when the teacher turns around, and no one can tell who threw it. You invest something with the desire and the wisdom, pack it up, and send it away, and it seems independent.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In the *nimshal* you have to flip this. In the *mashal*, if I let go of something, some of my force carries into it: if I throw a rock, it goes. In the *nimshal*, you have to think from the opposite direction: G-d wants to create an experience in which we feel separate. That is the idea of *Malchus* of *Malchus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: G-d has the ability and the desire to make us feel independent. The vessel He chooses is that the sun, the moon and the stars provide our needs, so the world is constantly changing and guided, yet it feels like natural phenomena. In that layer of reality there is just nature: we were thrown into the world on our own, a rock flying through space, and that there was a Big Bang, and everything was thrown a certain way.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We can understand how the planets and stars all function to do this, and how they can be a vessel that expresses the idea of giving us the feeling of independence. That is all we can really know.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The real essence of G-d's ability, to create a world that feels independent, could create a totally different universe, with no planets and no stars, where the beings are given energy and life by other mechanisms, and where even the fundamental laws of nature could be different. We cannot imagine that, and we certainly cannot understand the essence of that ability.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We cannot understand how G-d creates something from nothing and gives it the exact properties it needs. He sets up the laws of nature so the sun can cause nuclear fusion, which gives the energy, the light and the right wavelength to see by, the warmth, and the growth of plants. All of this is engineered from nothing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.question: Why is it this way and not another way? Where does that ability come from?
blocks.text: Much of this is totally hidden from us and beyond what anyone knows. Some of it is beyond what we know now but can be learned, and some of it is inherently beyond what created beings will ever know.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We have to recognize both sides. A person can really understand the science and the reality of how these things function: the created *yesh*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The phone with its icons
blocks.text: The created beings serve as an external vessel, a particular tool G-d uses to give us the sense of independence. By setting up the world this way, these things give us an illusion, a feeling that it is just going on its own. A *mashal* helps: imagine designing a phone or computer with graphic icons, so the user feels he is using tangible things, and touching a picture runs the code that makes it do what it does. Most of what happens is hidden from the user and has nothing to do with the pictures. It is set up that way so that it is easy to use. Most people are not aware of the technology that sends a cell phone or internet signal around the world.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In a similar way, G-d set up the world with this interface, which gives us the experience that our life comes from somewhere and that laws of reality are dictated to us like a king. Once they are given, they give us a sense of freedom, and we can be independent. This is how *Malchus* of *Malchus* is expressed in these *galgalim*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We can understand one side of the equation: how this *Malchus* is expressed in the *galgalim*. The other side is totally beyond anything we know. What is it like to create a universe from nothing? How does that work? We really have no idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and similarly

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: there's a similar kind of relationship of the *malachim* of *Beriya*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: where *bina* of *Atzilus*, which is called the mother, *Ima*, it says it like nests in *Beriya*, the world of *Beriya*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: שמשיגים כח האלה״י דמלכות דמלכות דאצילות כו'
phrases.en: So the *malachim* of *Beriya* are grasping, and in this sense grasping isn't like the way a human is understanding something; it's more the way something manifests or expresses something

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: So there is a certain way that *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is expressed in the *malachim* of *Beriya*, so they are grasping something of this G-dly source that creates them

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and so these angels, there's a certain aspect that they're able to grasp

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and that causes them to have this *hispaalus* from the greatness of the Creator

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: so we can understand how they are constantly nullified to their source

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב וצבא השמים לך משתחווים,
phrases.en: like it says, that the heavenly hosts bow down to you

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: like the physical things are *batel* when they are in their orbits, and then the higher angels are also nullified

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Similarly, the angels of *Beriya* have a relationship with *Atzilus*. *Bina* of *Atzilus*, which is called the mother, *Ima*, nests in *Beriya*, the world of *Beriya*, as it says. In that place the angels grasp the G-dly power of *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, which creates them.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: A painting that captures an idea
blocks.text: For the angels, grasping is not the way a human understands something. It is more the way something manifests or expresses it, as one says of a painting or a poem, "Oh, that captures this idea beautifully."

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The word *hasaga* can mean to grasp something intellectually, and it can also mean to capture something. In this sense the angels of *Beriya* capture and accurately express these G-dly ideas. *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is expressed in them, so they grasp something of the G-dly source that creates them.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is the *hasaga* of the angels: there is a certain aspect they are able to grasp, and it causes them *hispaalus*, to be moved by the greatness of the Creator.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We can also understand how they are constantly *batel* to their source, as it says, that the heavenly hosts bow down to You in their circling. The physical things are *batel* when they are in their orbits, and then the higher angels are also nullified.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In general, the angels of *Beriya* are *Torah* and *mitzvos*. The codified, formalized religion is the idea of the angel *Metatron*, the main angel of *Beriya*, and there are other, more particular angels of *Beriya* as well. These are *Torah* and *mitzvos* as a system and as logic, but their real essence is the G-dliness behind them.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The teacher's school system
blocks.text: A teacher or a parent wants to give a student the essentials: a love of learning, kindness, empathy and curiosity. To help bring that about, he builds a school with grades and tests and feedback, to motivate the student and give feedback on his achievement. That system is the *mashal* for the angels of *Beriya*, and the essential thing expressed in it is the light of *Atzilus*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So doing *Torah* and *mitzvos*, and understanding their logic and reasons as the *Gemara* describes them, are the angels of *Beriya*. The essential fact they express is G-d's desire, *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*. We can understand how these *mitzvos* are G-d's will, but the real essence of that will transcends these particular *mitzvos*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: They are only one external expression of it. The real essence is just whatever G-d wants us to do, and we will do it. As it says, if He told us to chop wood, we would chop wood. So a person has to recognize that the reason for a *mitzvah* is not its essence. The essence of the *mitzvah* is that it is G-d's will, which transcends logic, even the G-dly logic of the *Torah*, as we explained in the *kuntres* on the matter of Chassidus.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is only part of what G-d desires that we should have this independence in doing *Torah* and *mitzvos*: that we understand them, learn and apply the laws, and create our own courts. We are not to be robots. That is part of what G-d wants: that we understand His instructions and apply them with this logic and these rules.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The angels grasp something of *Malchus*, but its real essence transcends it. So in learning *Torah* you need two feelings: *bittul* to the Giver of the *Torah*, whose will transcends human logic, and yet He gives us the ability to understand and apply the laws on the logic He gave us. To the point that we do not listen even to a *bas kol*, the *beis din* follows its own understanding, and we cannot listen even to a *navi*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: The teacher who challenges his students
blocks.text: Sometimes a teacher gives students independence and instructions, and then he himself challenges them, but he wants them to stick to their original instructions. That is the idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The point is to recognize both sides. Part of it is understandable and systematic. Part of it is transcendent, and requires a sense of humility and awe and the recognition that it is really beyond us.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Similarly with the *bittul* of these external creations. The stars and planets all constantly orbit, and that is an expression of how they are nullified to their G-dly source, as it says that the heavenly hosts bow to You.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The simplest sense, the way the text describes it: the Shechina is in the east, and the fact that they go from east to west is like bowing, so to speak, to the Shechina.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: But I think the bigger idea is that they were invested with an unlimited force. Once they are thrown and set in motion, they keep going indefinitely. That is the idea of conservation of energy, and it shows that they are invested with a power higher than anything they have, not a finite power based on the normal rules of the universe.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It must be something higher, outside those normal rules, that can inject it, because within a finite system you can never make something that goes on indefinitely. So the constant orbit shows that the whole framework of reality is set up from something higher, and that they bump into this higher, underlying reality.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

sections.title: The hidden force behind Asiya: known only as hidden, and recognized as beyond everything we know
sections.summary: The transcendent force that creates the lowest world is hidden from our understanding. A person can recognize that it must be there, as the physicist recognizes a deeper reality behind the laws of nature, but its nature is not grasped.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת האין האלה״י דמלכות דעשיה המהווה,
phrases.en: but this g-dly transcendent force of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* that's creating everything

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: that is something that is hidden from our understanding, and we really don't know what that is, or its nature at least

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: רק שממילא הוא מוכרח בהשגה, אחר התאמת אופן הענין של ההתהוות היש כו'
phrases.en: it's just that we, our minds will recognize that it must be there

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: it's only so this g-dly source is only grasped in a very hidden way, just like being aware that there's something beyond me

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and it's recognized as being something that totally transcends anything that we know

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This transcendent force, the *Malchus* that creates everything, is hidden from our understanding. We really do not know what it is, or at least its nature.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Once one has grasped the manner in which the created *yesh* comes about, the mind recognizes that the transcendent source must be there.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A physicist today looks at the world and says that it is created in such a way, that the laws of nature hold up to a certain point. He can explain how gravity and electromagnetism work, and so how the planets and stars work.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: But why is it that way? We do not know. What sets it in motion? There must be a deeper reality behind all we see that causes it to be this way. It did not have to be this way; it is something like a choice, but we do not know what that is. We recognize a limit to our knowledge, and that there are things we are inherently beyond.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Books on the limits of knowledge
blocks.text: There are some great modern books on the unknown and the inherent limits of human knowledge. Some things we know are impossible for us to know. Some we do not know whether we could know. Some we hope, with more study, to figure out. But there is a line, and past it lies something beyond anything within our created existence.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This G-dly source is grasped only in a very hidden way: a person is aware that there is something beyond him, and that is all.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is recognized as something that totally transcends anything we know, which is what the wonder of it means.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

sections.title: Emanation in Atzilus: the lights and vessels, and the essence that shines through them
sections.summary: The same two sides apply to the details of *Atzilus*: its lights and vessels, the *chesed* and *chochma* that emanate, and the middos. Each can be grasped to a degree, but the essence of the emanator, which shines through them, is hidden and beyond all thought.

phrases.en: in a similar way

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: when we're studying the details

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: the lights and the vessels

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: for example

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: באצילות אור חסד שבמלכות או באצילות אור חסד שבחכמה
phrases.en: the emanation of the light of *chesed* of *Malchus* or the light of *chesed* of *chachma*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: So we can have some understanding of this idea of emanation, which is basically the idea of G-d's self-expression, how there's this expression of G-d's essence through these attributes

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: מאור הנאצל למטה בגילוי מהעלם העצמות
phrases.en: we can understand that through various metaphors like light, physical light, let's say, the light of the sun, or the way a person's soul is expressed, and things like that, from the essence that the hidden essence is being revealed and expressed in some way

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In a similar way, when a person studies the angels of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, he has to recognize both sides of them. The same applies to *yichuda ila'a* when studying the details of *Atzilus*, its lights and its vessels. For example, the emanation of the light of *chesed* of *Malchus*, or of *chesed* of *chachma*, and how it is emanated.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So we can understand this idea of emanation, which is G-d's self-expression: the hidden essence of G-d is expressed through these attributes. We can understand it through metaphors: physical light, like the light of the sun, or the way a person's soul is expressed. In this way the hidden essence is revealed and expressed in some way. This is what we have talked about before, and we will talk about more.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כמו ויאצל מן הרוח דמשה כו'
phrases.en: like it says, that Moshe emanated and gave some of his spirit to the elders

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: And so, in a similar way,

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ויושג גם כן בענין התהוות מדות דאצילות
phrases.en: and we can also understand something of how the *middos* of *Atzilus* are created

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: גם שהן בחינת מקוריים נבדלים מן השפעה האלהי״ת בנבראים כו'
phrases.en: even though that the *middos* of *Atzilus* are these spiritual forces and these spiritual sources which are totally, you know, transcend the physical, what the g-dly light is coming into creation

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Moshe's spirit given to the elders
blocks.text: As it says, Moshe emanated some of his spirit to the elders. Moshe did not change by doing that. He was able to inspire them, and they were able to express something of his character and his wisdom.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: In a similar way, G-d imbues these attributes, which are not G-d themselves, with the ability to become G-dly. They can become a G-dly kindness and a G-dly wisdom, and express the infinite, creative ability that is the hallmark of G-d, as opposed to human *chesed* and human *chochma*. So we can have some understanding of this idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We can also understand something of how the *middos* of *Atzilus* are created, even though they are spiritual sources that totally transcend the physical, and the G-dly light comes into creation through them. We can still understand them through these *meshalim*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: אבל בחינת אין האמיתי המאיר עליהם מאור עצמות המאצילם,
phrases.en: but the true G-dly *ayin*, the true G-d's true essence that is shining through and being expressed through those different attributes, the light of the essence of the emanator

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: that can't be understood even with this kind of comparison and metaphor

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: it's just something that we can recognize in this very hidden way that we know it's true

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: והוא בבחינת ראית השכל שלמעלה מן השגה ותפיסא ממש
phrases.en: and this is just that the mind sees it, and really this is like the soul seeing it, it's like *emuna*, that we can recognize, but it's in a way that's beyond true understanding and true grasp

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: וכמאמר לית מחשבה תפיסא בך כו',
phrases.en: like it says, that no thought can grasp You

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and this refers to the *machshava* of *bina*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: because seeing with *chachma* is really the opposite of understanding

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כי כל שמעמיק יותר, יותר מופלא הימנו עצמיות אור המאציל
phrases.en: because the deeper appreciation you have for this, what G-dliness really is, for the essence of the light of the emanator

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: what it means that G-d is really a G-d, and He's all-powerful and all these things, the more that you appreciate that, the more you recognize how it transcends any of our known limits, anything within time, anything within space, anything physical, even anything spiritual, and it just transcends

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: and the sign that a person does have this recognition of this G-dly essence is that

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: they have this deep sense of humility and awe and wonder, as opposed to this sense of feeling like, oh, I've got it in my back pocket in the sense of mastery

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: But the true *ayin*, the true essence of G-d shining through these different attributes, is the light of the essence of the emanator. We can appreciate, for example, that creating something from nothing is an expression of *chesed* of *Atzilus*. That is a G-dly *chesed*, because a person can give something to somebody, but cannot give them existence. Such giving is a G-dly giving, and it expresses a higher kind of thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: But *chesed* of *Atzilus* is only an example of G-d's essential ability: He is truly infinite and can do anything, and we cannot understand that at all, even through comparison. We can make a comparison between G-d's kindness and human kindness, and so we can understand the attributes in that way. But the real G-dly essence behind those attributes cannot be compared at all.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We recognize the essence only in a very hidden way. We know it is true, and our soul senses deeply, through *emuna*, that G-d has this essential, transcendent ability and is totally unlimited. We have that belief, but cannot really understand and explain it through our experiences. The mind sees it, and really it is the soul seeing it: *emuna*, which we can recognize, but beyond true understanding and true grasp.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: As it says, no thought can grasp You. The inner G-dly side of everything in the chain of worlds is transcendent and beyond human experience, and we cannot compare it. All our metaphors fail to grasp the true essence of the *nimshal*, so there is an aspect we cannot know at all.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This refers to the *machshava* of *bina*. The *machshava* of *bina* cannot grasp this side of the equation.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The seeing of *chachma* is the opposite of understanding. Understanding means creating a system, a framework and logic. Scientists who really know what they are talking about these days recognize that any logical theory you create, and in mathematics too, is only an effective theory: a useful model for certain aspects of reality, which can never grasp all of reality.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: By its very nature, any framework or model we create cannot grasp the true essence of reality, even physical reality. It certainly cannot grasp the transcendent reality of *chachma*, which is the recognition of an unlimited, creative possibility to do anything.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Learning to draw
blocks.text: Someone who has learned to draw is given paper and pencils, and told to create a work of art. He has a sense that he could make anything, but that sense cannot really be explained to anyone. When he actually draws, it is one particular drawing. The sense that he could do anything is inherently a transcendent experience.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So with G-dliness, even more so. We can recognize what He does in creation and appreciate some of its wisdom. But recognizing that whatever we see is an example of His higher, infinite ability means that He has an ability beyond anything we see and know. So it is beyond what we can grasp with *bina*, which creates a framework of comparisons and of the things we see and know.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This seeing of *chachma* is the opposite of understanding of *bina*. The deeper you appreciate what G-dliness is, the more you recognize how it transcends any limit we know: time, space, anything physical, even anything spiritual. The more you recognize that, the less you can use anything to build a framework for understanding. That is the nature of the *chachma* side of the equation.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The sign that a person has this recognition of the G-dly essence is that he has a deep *bittul*: a deep sense of humility, awe and wonder. That is the opposite of feeling that he has got it in his back pocket, in the sense of mastery. So you have to balance the two.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Newton and the seashore
blocks.text: Isaac Newton, I believe, has a quote: he felt like a child standing at the seashore of vast, infinite knowledge, and what he had was only a tiny drop. A healthy exploration of G-d's creation should always give a person this sense: I am mastering and knowing so much, but the more I know, the more I recognize that what I do not know is so much bigger and vaster than me.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That is the sign that a person has the *chachma* side of the equation in his radar and in his awareness.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

sections.title: Bittul and joy come together in every detail, in proportion to understanding
sections.summary: The two feelings from *chachma* and *bina* must come together in every detail a person studies, and they are proportional: the more he really understands, the more *bittul* he has. Imagined *bittul*, without understanding, is a vain fantasy.

phrases.he: ונמצא בחינת הביטול והשמחה שמסתעפים ונולדים מחכמה ובינה שבכל פרט,
phrases.en: So, therefore, it comes out that these two like emotional effects, these two feelings of both having the sense of humility and awe and wonder, and the joy and sense of satisfaction of mastery, that these which come from the *chachma* and *bina* type of perception

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.en: those should come together with every single detail that a person is studying

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: בכל התבוננות בכל פרט ופרט דווקא

phrases.en: and actually these two are interdependent

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ואם לא השמחה ביש מההשגה בטוב,
phrases.en: if a person doesn't have this joy, and this sense of accomplishment from really learning and knowing and mastering what you can know of G-d's creation

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: לא יבוא להפלאת וריחוק ההשגה באי''ן
phrases.en: then they're not really truly able to say that they appreciate the wonder, and have a real *bittul* and real *emuna* to G-d, and recognize how He transcends it

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: ולפי ערך השמחה כך ערך הביטול ממש,
phrases.en: And according to that *simcha*, that joy and that sense of accomplishment, exactly proportional to that, is going to be a person's *bittul*

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

phrases.he: כי כפי ערך ההשגה במתהווה, כך ערך ההפלאה בהבדל המהווה כו'
phrases.en: because according to how much a person understands the greatness of what G-d has created, that's going to give the person that sense of wonder and humility and *bittul* to the transcendence of the Creator and the force that's creating it

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So it comes out that these two feelings must come together. The *bittul* of humility, awe and wonder, and the *simcha* of the sense of mastery, both come from *chachma* and *bina*: *chachma* gives a person the sense of *bittul*, and *bina* gives the sense of *simcha*. They should come together with every single detail a person studies.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: When a person appreciates any aspect of creation, he should recognize the part he knows and gain real understanding and real mastery. He should not have only an indescribable spiritual experience, in which he gains nothing because it is not grounded. He should learn something he can know, explain and point to. On the other hand, he needs the wonder and *bittul* of recognizing the limits of what he does not know.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The two are interdependent, though they seem like opposites: each feeds the other. The sign that either is done properly is that it comes with the opposite side equally.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A person who lacks the joy of accomplishment from really learning what he can know of G-d's creation cannot truly say that he appreciates the wonder, has real *bittul* and *emuna*, or recognizes how G-d transcends it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: A person fools himself if he thinks he has this *bittul* and *emuna* while he cannot explain or point out the wonder of the works of creation. Then the other side of the feeling is not true either. That is why we have to do this type of learning and *hisbonenus*, so that the *chachma* perception is real and the *emuna* is internal and personal.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: According to the *simcha*, so is the *bittul*. The more a person understands the greatness of what G-d created, the more wonder and humility he has before the transcendence of the Creator and the force that creates it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The same is seen in any subject: whoever really studies a discipline is in awe of its masters, great musicians, artists or scientists, who did what they did so far beyond what others could do. This is true even just between humans.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: That awe comes only from really understanding what they did and why it is amazing: it comes from studying their works, what they taught and their way of life. The more one knows of the *Rebbe*, the *Rambam*, *Moshe Rabbeinu* or any of these *tzaddikim*, the more he recognizes how great they must be, and he cannot imagine what they were like.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: Thinking he is just a regular person

sensitivity.reason: Contempt for people who do not know or study the tzaddikim: "People with that ignorance", and their ignorant view of them.
sensitivity.publishable: Someone who knows nothing about them, and does not study them, thinks, "They're just a regular Joe Schmo like me." People without that knowledge often feel, "What's the big deal? They're some holy dude, basically like me." It takes intimate knowledge to create a sense of proportion and wonder, to recognize that this comes from someone beyond the regular person, and to realize in the end that he is incomparably beyond me.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The mockery of the ignorant view is his. The flagged words are the contempt in "ignorance"; the point (intimate knowledge gives proportion) stands in both texts. A person decides whether the contempt prints.

blocks.text: Someone who knows nothing about them, and does not study them, thinks, "They're just a regular Joe Schmo like me." People with that ignorance often feel, "What's the big deal? They're some holy dude, basically like me." It takes intimate knowledge to create a sense of proportion and wonder, to recognize that this comes from someone beyond the regular person, and to realize in the end that he is incomparably beyond me.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The *Rebbe* would often say that the difference between a small child and a great professor or scientist is still a matter of degree, since the child can grow into that. Here we are talking about a created being and the Creator, which creates an even greater sense of awe and *bittul*.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: We throw the word G-d around all the time, but if a person does not really study, he does not know whom he is talking about. So we cannot have the proper reverence, *bittul* and awe without appreciating the greatness and vastness of His works.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is a great general principle to bear in mind when studying any detail: a chapter of *Shaar HaYichud*, some *hisbonenus*, a *sichah* or a *maamar*, or any study of *Kabbalah*, such as the *Zohar* or the *Arizal*. It always has to be within this framework.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Whether one focuses on every detail or on the general big picture, one must keep both sides. One has to make sure one's understanding is real, that one is really learning something that one can point to and master. Together with that, one should realize that it comes from somewhere beyond, so that one does not become arrogant and feel that he has mastered it. If a person sees both sides, it gives him true *bittul*, humility and awe.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The parenthesis is about what happens when a person lacks the balance between the two. If someone just imagines that he has grasped the creation very well, but lacks *bittul* before the Creator, he surely did not understand anything.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So a person can learn *Chassidus* and *Kabbalah* and feel that he masters them, because he can say a lot of words and talk about a lot of levels. But if it did not lead him to *bittul*, to wonder and humility before the source, it shows that he is not understanding what is going on at all.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Others are interested in feeding their ego, or they come to it without proper training. They gain enough knowledge and enough words to sound intelligent and feel like an authority, but they do not have true understanding. So they do not have the proper respect and awe for what they are talking about, because they lack the perspective of what all this really means.

sensitivity.reason: Attributes to a group of people ("Others") a motive, feeding their ego, and calls them intelligent-sounding but without true understanding.
sensitivity.publishable: Some come to it without proper training. They gain enough knowledge and enough words to sound intelligent and feel like an authority, but they do not have true understanding. So they do not have the proper respect and awe for what they are talking about, because they lack the perspective of what all this really means.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The description of learners without understanding is his point and stays. The flagged words are the ego motive attributed to "Others". A person decides whether the sneer at their authority prints.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is important to recognize that someone who claims to be a big expert, and says a lot of words, but does not have that *bittul*, shows that he is misguided and is not really studying it properly. He does not really understand it.

sensitivity.reason: Contempt for a type of person who claims to be an expert in Chassidus ("a big expert", "misguided").
sensitivity.publishable: It is important to recognize that someone who says a lot of words, but does not have that *bittul*, shows that he is not really studying it properly. He does not really understand it.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The point, that words without bittul show weak study, is his and stays. The flagged words are the claim to be an expert and "misguided". A person decides whether they print.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: When you have the opposite, a person can imagine that he has great *bittul* and great *emuna*. There is a natural *emuna* that the soul has, which is a gift, though even that needs to be activated through some *hisbonenus*. But this real inner *bittul*, which is inside the mind and heart, can only come from real understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: So if a person feels that he has that *bittul*, but did not properly grasp the greatness of the creation and how it relates to the Creator, he cannot explain it. Sometimes people learn *Chassidus*, and it turns on the external aspect of the soul's *emuna*. They feel uplifted and they feel they have great *bittul*, but they do not really understand it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: They talk about *Atzilus* and high levels like *Adam Kadmon*, and it is very great and exciting in a certain way, and spiritually uplifting because of its abstractness. The Alter Rebbe's *maamar* describes this spiritual sickness: getting excited by general, abstract spiritual ideas without grounding them in true understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.title: A study partner's question
blocks.text: Then you ask: what is *Atzilus* at the table? How do I see this in life? A study partner of his, very earthy and grounded, would always say, "Why should I care?" Sometimes it was a frustrating question, but it is the question we need to ask ourselves.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: How do I see this in the world around me? Why should I care about it? How is this something I can relate to? If a person does not have that understanding in a tangible way in the world around him, then his *bittul* is not going to be true either.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: It is a vain imagination and a fantasy, and such people have no real *bittul* at all. It is really a veiled arrogance, making them think that they are spiritual and close to G-d, because they want to be, and they feel it is a noble thing. So they try to imitate it, like little kids imitate adults. But it is not a real thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

sensitivity.reason: Contempt for people who study Chassidus and claim spiritual attainment: "veiled arrogance", imitating "like little kids".
sensitivity.publishable: It is a vain imagination and a fantasy, and such people have no real *bittul* at all. It makes them think that they are spiritual and close to G-d, because they want to be, and they feel it is a noble thing. So they try to imitate it. But it is not a real thing.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The contempt is aimed at a group of students of Chassidus. A person decides whether the "veiled arrogance" words print as said.

blocks.text: The two are totally interdependent. With any subject: a person who is going to be a doctor must really understand the subject and study the body; someone building a bridge had better know his engineering. He cannot just feel one with the universal laws of nature. So with connection to G-d, it requires real study of these topics, and the *bittul* is proportional to how much a person understands, for the reason explained above.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: There is a kind of *makif* *bittul* that comes from action, from training and from environment, and it has certain advantages. But here we are talking about the inner *bittul*, the *avodah* that happens within the mind and heart. That kind of *bittul* requires understanding, and there is no way around that.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: Sometimes a person gets a spark of G-dly inspiration from above, which is a *makif* type of thing. But to have it internalized, as real feelings in the mind and the heart, that can only come through real understanding and real study. There is no other way around it.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is known to all who have tasted a true *hisbonenus* and experienced the real thing. Once you have tasted it, you know what it is and you cannot go back. Such people do not fool themselves at all. They recognize what is really going on.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: This is well known to those who are accustomed to the ways of *Chassidus* from their youth. They were guided to know the true path and not to fool themselves: the difference between just this kind of *makif* type of *emuna* and upbringing, and real inner understanding and feelings.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: But unfortunately a lot of people, I guess the majority of people, even fool themselves when it comes to all of this, and there are all sorts of ways that people delude themselves. In general there is a big lack of guidance. No one is really teaching this type of thing, though some people do study these kinds of books.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: One of the earliest books written specifically about this is the *Chovos HaLevavos*, *Duties of the Heart*. In it the author laments that people do not focus on and study these inner aspects of religion. A person can pay lip service, saying "Yes, I believe in G-d", because he was trained to say it. But it does not mean anything unless he understands what he believes in.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: What does it mean that G-d is one? "Of course there's one G-d, I believe in monotheism." But what does that really mean? A person who does not study G-d's unity says he believes it, but does not really know what he is saying or believing.

audio.lecture: Walters 2020 Edited/Shaar HaYichud/Ch 05/Shaar HaYichud 047 ch 5 part 2.mp3

blocks.text: The same is true of love and fear of G-d and the other inner feelings. They can only be born through really studying these ideas, the greatness of G-d's creation and handiwork. Putting all that together gives us the real *avodah pnimis*, which is a big fundamental thing in Judaism generally, and especially emphasized in *Chassidus*, and especially in *Chassidus Chabad*.

notes.text: Class 047 line 28 is read "of Malchus of Atzilus" where the chapter line reads Asiya. The teacher's words are kept as said; the reviewer may want to check the tape.

Class 047 w4027: the transcript gives an unclear word in its place ("the [unclear] liked to call the laws of creation"). Unclear who is meant, so the name is left out and the block says only "the laws of nature".

The Tanya aside on the impurity of secular wisdom is flagged other-groups (judgment). Tanya's impurity is quoted as he gives it. The flagged link to secular wisdom is replaced in the publishable text ("that can come with learning"). His gloss, which he marks as his own ("I think"), is written "Rabbi Walters thinks" in both texts, so that it stays his opinion.

Criticism of people is flagged where it is contempt for an unnamed group: "Others are interested in feeding their ego" (the block after the Chassidus and Kabbalah passage), "a big expert ... misguided", "People with that ignorance" (the aside on the tzaddikim, line 41 or 42), and "veiled arrogance" with "like little kids" (the block on people who imitate it, line 46). Not flagged: his description of people who learn Chassidus and feel bittul without understanding it, and "a lot of people ... fool themselves" (line 48), which describe a state rather than insult. A reviewer may decide otherwise.

The study-partner recollection ("Why should I care?") is the teacher's own, with no name and no circumstances beyond the trait of being earthy and grounded. Not flagged private; a reviewer may decide.

Hedges kept: "Rabbi Walters thinks" (the Tanya gloss on line 6, and bittul as mainly awe on line 15), "But I think the bigger idea" (conservation of energy, line 27), "I believe" (the Newton quote, line 38), "I guess the majority of people" (line 48). Dropped: "I don't know" and similar tics.

Hebrew-only phrases (he reads them with no English of his of their own; where he gives English, it is in the block): line 2 (a clause he reads without rendering); the closing 'etc.' of lines 4, 8, 12, 15 and 16; the clause on line 32 that is read and glossed by the block only; the clause on line 39 ('as explained above'); the phrase on line 41 ('every single detail'), whose English comes in the phrase before it; the clause on line 47 ('for the reason'), followed by 'for this reason we've explained'; and the closing 'etc.' of line 48 and of line 49.
